sections.h2: Who bills property tax on a Bloomington house?
sections.html:
McLean County bills it. Bloomington is the county seat, and the county treasurer and tax collector sends one bill per parcel on behalf of nearly 200 taxing districts, covering about 68,000 parcels. That office works from the Government Center, 115 E. Washington Street, Room M101, and answers at (309) 888-5180.

Assessment is a separate job. The City of Bloomington Township assessor values property inside the city, the county Supervisor of Assessments (the chief county assessment officer) handles equalization and exemptions at (309) 888-5130, and the county Board of Review hears complaints. The city government itself does not send a property tax bill, though it registers rental buildings and collects its own local taxes.

  • County treasurer: payments, duplicate bills, delinquent tax and the annual tax sale.
  • Township assessor and county assessor: values, property record cards, exemptions and address changes.
  • Board of Review: assessment complaints, reached at (309) 888-5132.

sections.h2: What is Bloomington like for someone selling a home?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 78,680 people, placing Bloomington 13th among Illinois cities and fifth outside the Chicago area. It sits beside Normal, and the pair anchor a metro of roughly 170,000 people. The town dates to 1831 and was named seat when McLean County was created. Illinois Wesleyan University, State Farm and Country Financial are major local institutions, and Beer Nuts snacks are made only here.

Interstates 39, 55 and 74 meet at Bloomington, with US 51, US 150 and Illinois Route 9 also passing through. Two public systems serve the city, Bloomington District 87 and McLean County Unit District 5, and small portions reach into Olympia District 16. Weather runs from a January average low near 14 degrees to a July high near 86.

  • The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 78,804 residents, a 0.1% rise since 2020.
  • Owners live in 61.9% of occupied homes, so roughly 38 in 100 are rented, which matters if you sell to an investor.
  • Typical owned homes are valued at $203,300, and renters pay a median of $1,050 a month.
  • Median household income of $77,384 and a 16.8-minute average commute.

sections.h2: When are McLean County tax bills due?
sections.html:
McLean County's treasurer states that taxes are always due in the first week of June and the first week of September. For 2026 the dates were June 10 and September 10, and the treasurer posts that all dates are subject to change. The county says a person who never receives a bill is still liable under 35 ILCS 200/20-15, and asks owners without a bill by mid-May to call for a duplicate.

McLean County 2026 collection calendar for tax year 2025 (source: McLean County Treasurer)
DateEvent
May 7Real estate bills scheduled to be mailed
June 10First installment due
September 10Second installment due
October 9Last day to pay in the office by personal check
October 12$10.00 certified fee and delinquency letters
November 5Judgment hearing; last day to pay to avoid the sale
November 6Delinquent tax sale begins at 10:00 a.m.

Those 2026 dates are all in the past. Late payments carry interest of 1.5% per month, starting the day after the due date, and a payment postmarked by the due date is on time.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Bloomington property tax bill?
sections.html:
The treasurer lists several routes. Partial payments are not accepted, and no receipt is mailed unless you ask, since a canceled check or bank statement stands in as proof.

  • By mail to the lockbox: McLean County Collector, P.O. Box 843637, Kansas City, MO 64184-3637.
  • In person at 115 E. Washington Street, Monday to Friday, 8:00 until 4:30.
  • At a drop box, open around the clock, on the Washington Street side of the lot or at the East Street entrance.
  • Online or by phone with a credit card, with a convenience fee, or through annual automatic withdrawal.
  • At a participating local bank.

After October 9, the office requires certified funds for payments, and no payments are taken on the day of the sale. A mortgage company asking for a duplicate bill pays a $5.00 fee under state law. If you refinanced or paid off a mortgage, file a change of address with the Supervisor of Assessments so future bills reach you.

sections.h2: How can a Bloomington owner challenge an assessment?
sections.html:
An owner has 30 days after the township's notice appears in the newspaper to file a complaint with the Board of Review. For 2026, the City of Bloomington Township notice ran in the Pantagraph on September 29 with a filing deadline of October 29 and an equalization factor of 1.0385. Bloomington Township, a separate township in the same county, had the same dates and a factor of 1.0534. Check which township your parcel is in before you rely on either number.

The county explains that the assessment reflects the past three years of market value before January 1 of the assessment year, and an equalization factor is applied to bring the result to 33.33%. A late complaint will not be heard. Owners use form PTAX-230 for nonfarm property, and the Board meets in the Supervisor of Assessments' office in the Government Center. The Board's 2026 schedule ran from June into mid-December.

Following the severe storms of June 30, 2026, McLean County was named in a state disaster declaration, which lets owners apply for reassessment on form PTAX-245. A second declaration followed on August 18, 2026. Owners of storm-damaged homes should ask the assessor whether that process applies.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions apply in McLean County?
sections.html:
Exemptions reduce the taxable value before the rate is applied, so the dollar saving depends on your tax rate. Only a primary residence qualifies, and the county's own page lists these:

  • General homestead: up to $6,000, filed first with the chief county assessment officer.
  • Homestead improvement: up to $75,000 of market value, or $25,000 assessed, usually granted automatically for four years.
  • Senior citizens: $5,000, with an initial PTAX-324 and proof of age.
  • Low-income senior freeze: household income under $75,000, using PTAX-340, which the county mails each year around February 1 to current senior exemption holders.
  • Disabled persons: $2,000, renewed yearly with the county's December 31 due date.
  • Returning veterans: $5,000 for the year the veteran returns and the following year.
  • Disabled veterans: $2,500, $5,000 or up to $250,000, depending on the rating.

The senior deferral program is run through the treasurer at (309) 888-5180. A buyer must file their own claims after closing.

sections.h2: What rules does the city add for rental houses?
sections.html:
An investor selling a rental should know that the City of Bloomington requires every owner of residential rental property inside the city limits to register it each year. Its Rental Property Program prints a fee of $65 per building, plus $5 per unit in buildings with three or more units, and registrations run through December 31.

The city states that a registration cannot be transferred to a new owner, so a buyer registers again. It also states that no one may rent or occupy a covered building without a Certificate of Inspection. A building rated "fair" may need a $5,000 letter of credit or pledged account until it passes, and follow-up inspections are charged at $100 per appointment. A missed inspection costs $75. Fix any open violations before you list, since they affect a buyer's repair requests.

faqs.q: Which office do I call about a Bloomington property tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the McLean County treasurer at (309) 888-5180 for payments and duplicate bills, and the county assessor at (309) 888-5130 for values, exemptions and mailing addresses. The city of Bloomington does not send the bill.

faqs.q: When is the second installment of Bloomington property tax due?
faqs.a: It falls in the first week of September each year. For 2026 the county listed September 10. Interest of 1.5% per month starts the day after the due date.

faqs.q: Did Bloomington taxpayers have a deadline to appeal in 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Bloomington Township filing deadline was October 29, 2026, thirty days after its September 29 notice. That date has passed, so watch for next year's newspaper notice.

faqs.q: Does Bloomington require rental registration when I sell?
faqs.a: Registration belongs to the owner, and the city says it cannot transfer to a new owner. A buyer of a rental registers anew and pays the printed fee of $65 per building.

faqs.q: Can I pay McLean County tax with a card?
faqs.a: Yes, online or by phone, with a convenience fee. The office also accepts mail, in-person payments, a 24-hour drop box, local banks and annual automatic withdrawal.
